title: Development of a biaxial tensile testing machine for pulsed neutron experiments
author: Kiriyama, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: Install and configure BTM‑NEU
steps.instruction: Mount the biaxial tensile testing machine for neutron experiments (BTM‑NEU) on the RADEN sample stage so that its base is at 1.773 m height from the floor; verify machine dimensions (1475 mm × 1450 mm × 415 mm) and weight (1390 kg) fit the stage; connect the dedicated control system (independent of RADEN) and synchronize both systems with an external timer; confirm load capacity of 50 kN per direction, cross‑head speed range 0.001–60 mm/min, displacement accuracy ≤1 % of the 85 mm set value, and data sampling rate 1–200 Hz.

substeps.instruction: Secure the machine to the stage using the provided mounting brackets.
Power on the BTM‑NEU controller and the RADEN data acquisition system.
Set up the external timer to provide a common time base for both systems.

steps.title: Prepare specimen and clamps
steps.instruction: Select an ISO‑standardized cruciform specimen (arm length 130 mm, arm width 30 mm, thickness 0.5–10 mm) or a non‑ISO/strip specimen meeting the same size limits; place the specimen in the centre of the BTM‑NEU and fix it with the 4 mm‑thick clamps, ensuring the white square aperture aligns with the neutron beam path; orient the specimen so that its rolling direction is parallel to the X‑direction of the machine.

steps.title: Attach strain gauges for biaxial tests
steps.instruction: Bond two Showa strain gauges (Y11‑MA‑1‑120‑11‑P4‑L005‑BSS) on the cruciform specimen, one in the X‑direction and one in the Y‑direction, each positioned 10.5 mm from the centre; for uniaxial tests, attach a single Kyowa gauge (KFGS‑1N‑120‑C1‑11) at the centre of the specimen.

steps.title: Run biaxial tensile tests at nine stress ratios
steps.instruction: Program the BTM‑NEU to apply the following stress‑ratio sets (σx:σy): 1:0, 4:1, 2:1, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 1:2, 1:4, 0:1; for each ratio set the loading rate to 125 N s⁻¹ (7.5 kN min⁻¹) in load‑control mode; record load, displacement and strain data at the chosen sampling rate (1–200 Hz) until failure or the desired strain is reached; compute true stress σt = σn(1+εn) and true strain εt = ln(1+εn) where σn = P/A0 and εn is the engineering strain.

steps.title: Configure long‑time biaxial test for neutron imaging
steps.instruction: Set the stress ratio to 1:1 and select load‑control mode; apply a loading rate of 333.3 N s⁻¹ (20 kN min⁻¹); execute the following load‑hold sequence: 0 kN for 20 h (non‑loading), increase to 20 kN and hold for 23.5 h, increase to 45 kN and hold for 23.5 h, then unload to 0 kN and hold for 23.5 h (post‑unloading), giving a total test time of 90.5 h; do not attach strain gauges to the central region during this test to avoid perturbing the neutron transmission.

steps.title: Measure strain distribution during long‑time test
steps.instruction: Place nine Kyowa strain gauges (KFGS‑1N‑120‑C1‑11) on the specimen surface along the X‑direction, spaced 7.5 mm apart, covering the central 30 mm × 30 mm area; record strain continuously throughout each load condition of the long‑time test; later calculate mean strain and standard deviation for each load.

steps.title: Perform in‑situ Bragg‑edge neutron imaging trial
steps.instruction: Install the BTM‑NEU in the RADEN beamline; set the proton‑beam power for neutron production to 150 kW; irradiate the central 30 mm × 30 mm region of the specimen with the pulsed neutron beam while maintaining the same load sequence as the long‑time test (0 kN, 20 kN, 45 kN, 0 kN) with a 5 h hold at each load; collect neutron transmission spectra with the GEM‑type area detector; analyse the α‑Fe {110} Bragg‑edge using the RITS code to obtain the thickness‑direction lattice strain for each load condition; average the spectra over the central area to improve signal‑to‑noise.
